title: U.S. House · Florida's 15th District
area: West-central Florida, including parts of Hillsborough and Polk counties east of Tampa.

context.text: The Republican primary was canceled and incumbent Laurel Lee advanced unopposed. Robert People won the Democratic primary with 53.7% of the vote against Christopher Irizarry.

candidates.name: Laurel Lee

priorities.text: Education: says she supports school choice and wants to ensure families have the resources to pursue an education that fits their needs.
priorities.quote: I understand the importance of school choice in order to empower families to make decisions that will provide their children with the best education possible.

priorities.text: Economy: says she wants to lower taxes, balance the budget, and remove regulations she says burden small businesses.
priorities.quote: I will work to lower taxes on you and your family, balance the budget, and remove regulations that harm Florida’s small businesses.

priorities.text: Law enforcement: says she supports fully funding police and opposes "defund the police" rhetoric and policies.
priorities.quote: I strongly oppose “defund the police” rhetoric and policies.

positions.summary: Says she is a strong supporter of the Second Amendment and will fight efforts that might infringe on gun owners' rights.
positions.quote: I am a strong supporter of the Second Amendment, and I will always fight to protect the constitutional rights of law-abiding gun owners from efforts that might infringe on their right to keep and bear arms.

positions.summary: Says she opposes "defund the police" policies and will support legislation that fully funds law enforcement.
positions.quote: I will always support legislation that fully funds our law enforcement and equips them with the resources they need to keep our streets and communities safe.

positions.summary: Cosponsored H.R. 22, the SAVE Act (119th Congress).

record.text: Assigned to chair the Committee on House Administration's Elections Subcommittee and serve as Vice Chair of the full Committee on House Administration and the Joint Committee on the Library, plus seats on the Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Committee on Judiciary, for the 2025-2026 Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: Lee has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; positions and priorities are drawn from her official House issues pages, which cover only a subset of the 15 tracked issues.

candidates.name: Robert People

priorities.text: Protecting Social Security, including a proposal that the government return "full amounts" it has collected to beneficiaries.
Women's reproductive and health rights, including reversing what he calls "harmful policies" on abortion access.
Raising teacher salaries, starting with District 15, by shifting county school-budget funds away from what he calls wasteful spending.

candidates.researchNotes: Based on his 2025 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no campaign website or other public statements were found. His survey does not address other guide issues.

statements.quote: I want to start by reversing the harmful policies in place, especially regarding abortion.
statements.context: In his 2025 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

statements.quote: requiring ICE agents to identify themselves FULLY and to treat detainees as human beings (unlike what is taking place now), proposing the destruction of the "Alligator Alley" detention facility
statements.context: In his 2025 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

candidates.name: Angie Boone
candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia biography page, campaign website, or completed Candidate Connection survey was found for Boone in the time available. A further search found only her Florida Division of Elections write-in qualification record (June 12, 2026).
